text:
support_cecilia: Customer (acme-inc) opened an escalation — p99 spike on streaming endpoints after last runtime deploy. Non-stream endpoints look fine. TTFB for streaming ~600-900ms p99 (baseline ~120ms). Total time for small responses ~similar to baseline. attaching perf snapshot: https://perf.redwood/abc123 :eyes:

raj_oncall: Can you paste a minimal repro (curl + headers) + client (node/python) and whether they're using SSE or h2? Need to rule out client/proxy buffering.

support_cecilia: Repro curl we used:
```
curl -i -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams?model=redwood/fast-infer-4b-8bit&prompt=hello"
```
Server logs show first_chunk_sent at ~+0.62s. Snippet:
```
[2026-03-16T14:02:03Z] req=abc start
[2026-03-16T14:02:03Z] req=abc kernel_select=0.12s
[2026-03-16T14:02:03Z] req=abc batch_wait=0.40s
[2026-03-16T14:02:03Z] req=abc first_chunk_sent=0.62s size=64
```
Client is node-sdk v0.9.1 behind company proxy (nginx -> envoy).

mike_runtime: Two likely categories: 1) runtime-level hold (batching/flush heuristics / min-chunks), 2) network/proxy buffering until chunk threshold. Also quantized model + small prompt can mean longer kernel prep/warmup. Which model + prompt len?

support_cecilia: Model: redwood/fast-infer-4b-8bit, prompt ~40 tokens. Other customers on same model not affected, seems tenant-specific path.

sophie_devex: If nginx/envoy buffers, nginx opts: `proxy_buffering off; proxy_http_version 1.1; chunked_transfer_encoding on;` help. For Envoy you need `per_connection_buffer_limit_bytes` and disable `streaming_filter` that aggregates. Ask customer to test bypassing their proxy.

raj_oncall: Quick internal note: we rolled a change 48h ago that bumped streaming `min_chunks` from 1 -> 2 for quantized models to reduce tiny-chunk noise. That would introduce an extra wait for the first flush in short-response cases. Could be the regression.

support_cecilia: Runtime traces align: kernel_select ~120ms + batching wait ~400ms. First-chunk delayed specifically. Non-streaming p99 total is ~350ms, so streaming TTFB ~720ms vs total ~760ms — initial chunk is the problem.

mike_runtime: Good repro. Two immediate mitigation paths: (A) enable tenant-level override to force immediate flush (min_chunks=1 / flush-immediate) for acme-inc; (B) rollback the min_chunks change. Also add first-chunk latency metric.

marcus_ml: We shipped that change to reduce tiny-chunk noise, but for quantized models this interacts poorly with short prompts. Agree tenant override defaulting to 1 for high-SLO customers is safest. I'll prep a quick config patch.

support_cecilia: Customer says they can run a direct test (bypass their proxy) later today. Will coordinate. Meanwhile they asked for a short-lived workaround on our side.

raj_oncall: I'll create rollback + override plan. If we can enable override only for acme-inc, do that first as lower-risk. I'll also add a canary at 5%.

mike_runtime: I'll open INF-4451 and PR #890 to add tenant flag and rollout steps. Also instrument `first_chunk_latency_ms` p50/p95/p99.

ops-bot: [deployment] PR #890 deployed to canary (5%) at 16:30 UTC.

mike_runtime: Canary numbers: first-chunk p95 improved 480ms -> 140ms, p99 improved 720ms -> 160ms for canary traffic. No regressions observed in memory/throughput so far.

sophie_devex: Share repro snippets we gave customer (lightweight):
Node:
```
const s = await client.stream({model:'redwood/fast-infer-4b-8bit', prompt:'hi'})
s.on('data', d => console.log('chunk', d))
```
Curl:
`curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams?model=...`

support_cecilia: Customer bypassed their proxy and confirmed TTFB dropped to ~140ms. They're happy to wait for full rollout. Marking as resolved after canary -> full. :pray:

mike_runtime: Rolling to 100% in 30m if no new alerts. I'll follow up with a postmortem on how min_chunks interacts with quantized models.

support_cecilia: Thanks everyone — will update ticket and close once 100% done. :thumbsup:
